title: Claude Max Automation: What It Covers and Costs (2026)
summary: Claude Max automation uses subscription features like Claude apps and Code, while custom scripts and workflow tools are billed separately per token.
body_markdown:
## Automate across other apps with Activepieces


Activepieces suits event-triggered jobs that span several apps, with 747 integrations counted in its open source repo, but it calls Claude through the API, billed per token, so it adds a second cost that your Max subscription doesn't cover.


Its platform fee's a third line on top of that, though flows are unlimited on every plan, including free.


### A sample workflow


In the screenshot below, a small flow named "Test Flow" starts with a weekly schedule trigger, a Google Sheets step pulls the next rows from an "Invoice" spreadsheet's "Bill reminder" sheet beginning at row 2, and a loop step handles each row.


The highlighted configuration shows how plain the setup is: a connection, a sheet and a start row. Nothing in it needs Claude yet, which is the point. Add a Claude step to the loop and each row becomes a billable API call.


### What it costs


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) has a free plan with unlimited flows, self-serve Plus and Team plans at $20 and $200 a month, and custom-priced Ultimate and Embed plans through sales (pricing checked 2026-10-23).


For one weekly flow, the free plan's 1,000 credits a month can cover the platform side before a single token is spent. None of these plans includes Claude usage, so the real cost per run is the platform fee spread over your runs, plus tokens.


If a task lives inside Claude, a scheduled task or Claude Code covers it under Max, and no platform fee applies.


Reach for Activepieces when something in one app, such as a new spreadsheet row, must trigger work in another; a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, and with your own Anthropic key on Plus or above, the Claude step is 1 credit while the token cost lands on your own provider bill.


Cost per run then depends on your volume, so work it out before you build.
